feed.title: NPR Topics: Business
feed.subtitle: Reporting on the money that flows through our economy, from Wall Street financial firms to Silicon Valley tech giants, small businesses, consumers, employers and workers. Plus podcast episodes of Planet Money and The Indicator.

entry.title: Nvidia tries to get back to business
entry.summary: Nvidia quarterly earnings are in. But the biggest question isn't about past business performance it's about the company's future leadership.

entry.title: Nvidia board says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
entry.summary: The former Nvidia CEO said he would be "honored" to return if the board allowed. But the board says it has no intention of reinstating him.

entry.title: Can Google win the AI race without killing its cash cow?
entry.summary: In late October, Google had the worst stock day in its history as a public company. The Planet Money newsletter asks: has Google been caught in "the innovator's dilemma"?

entry.title: She went to college to become a social worker. Now she's joined the skilled trades
entry.summary: While the rise of AI continues to fuel the debate over whether college is worth the cost, apprenticeships in the skilled trades are having a moment, drawing in people of all backgrounds including college graduates.

entry.title: New rule aims to close loophole on chip exports
entry.summary: The Commerce Department released a new rule designed to make it harder for China to gain access to America's most powerful computer chips using third-country data centers.

entry.title: Commerce Department under pressure for delaying export controls on Nvidia chips
entry.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department is under scrutiny for clearing Chinese companies to handle Nvidia chips, despite national security concerns from cabinet officials and U.S. intelligence agencies.

entry.title: These economists say in-person work boosts creativity, but office mandates fall short
entry.summary: A pair economists argue in a new book that people are more creative and productive when they work together in person. But it's not enough for employers to simply order workers back to the office.

entry.title: Is there an opening for Nvidia's competitors, now that Jensen Huang is out?
entry.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow talks with Dylan Patel of the AI and semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis about Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, and whether it opens up the field for Nvidia's competitors.

entry.title: Does Europe regret its bet on U.S. defense?
entry.summary: Europe bet big on American defense technology and they're now paying the price. Years-long backlogs are underway due to production delays and the U.S. own military needs.

entry.title: SpaceX's giant rocket may leave NASA in the dust
entry.summary: As it races to develop its new massive rocket, the space launch company is preparing to retire NASA's main ride to the International Space Station.
